To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the perception of the traditional community regarding the research conducted in coastal environment is not satisfactory; (2) the traditional communities are unaware of the results of the research and the management actions that may be implemented; (3) the traditional community is unaware of the research being conducted and the results obtained; (4) there is a lack of dialogue between the researchers and the traditional community, which can result not only in the loss of research results but also in the credibility of the research itself.

there is a lack of communication and integration between researchers and traditional communities, and this lack of integration results in conflicts between those directly involved, reduced management measures and a loss of research credibility.
the dialogue between researchers and local communities is essential for the development of coastal management strategies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the integration of scientific and traditional knowledge, which is a challenge for the future of coastal management.
the importance of integrating traditional knowledge and scientific research in coastal management.
the importance of integration between scientific knowledge and the traditional knowledge of coastal communities to the management of coastal areas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dialogue between researchers and fishermen in the PEC is not effective, and there is a need to improve the communication channels to promote the integration of scientific and traditional knowledge in the region.
the dialogue between scientific and traditional communities is essential for a better understanding of the problems of coastal management.

traditional communities should be included in the decision-making processes of the protected areas and that research should be conducted in partnership with traditional communities, in which the results are discussed with the local community before being presented to managers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the integration of traditional knowledge with scientific knowledge can be a tool for better management of the coastal environment.
the integration of traditional knowledge and science is essential in the management of marine protected areas.
traditional knowledge should be integrated with scientific knowledge in order to improve the conservation of the coastal environment.

the integration of traditional and scientific knowledge in the PEC is essential for the sustainable management of the marine resources.
the integration between traditional knowledge of the communities and scientific knowledge is essential for the management of the coastal zone.
the integration of scientific and traditional knowledge in coastal management can be a key element in the search for effective solutions for the conservation of the coastal environment.
